tables.title: Joint Construction of the Continuum and the Constants
tables.intro: Generation begins in the arithmetic nucleus and preserves the sequence of its transformations. The coordinates π, φ, e, and α belong to the same genealogy; conventional values are not introduced as generating data. Sources: article I and the time-crystal monograph.

rows.name: Arithmetic Nucleus, Orientation, and Memory
rows.explanation: APP compares addition and multiplication over the alphabet 1,…,9 in two orientations; TRIT preserves the three local regimes, and TPK incorporates phase, memory, and carry. The census traverses 104,976 ordered pairs of oriented cursors (324²), distinguishes 468 emissions, and obtains 243 ternary images within an ambient set of 729 elements. Each number counts objects at a different level.

rows.name: Compatible Prolongation and the Nonadic Connection
equations: $w_6\longrightarrow w_{12}\longrightarrow w_{18}\longrightarrow w_{24}\longrightarrow w_{30}\longrightarrow R_{36}\longrightarrow G_9$
rows.explanation: The L₀ lifts lead to w12 and w18; the L₁ lifts change regime at w24 and w30 while preserving prefix, orientation, and memory. R36 opens the coinductive boundary, and G9 brings together nine local domains. The holonomy Γ9 represents a complete turn: phase returns and the memory counter advances. The monodromic representation preserves this displacement between turns; even when the 108-position calendar is restored, accumulated memory remains. Nested cylinders determine the coordinates through compatible prolongation.

rows.name: Sturmian Order and Vacancies
rows.explanation: The comparison of ternary and decimal capacities produces an aperiodic Sturmian reading. Its events are separated by 21 or 22 steps; the distribution of short intervals induces a second scale of 6 or 7. A vacancy adds a block to the record without increasing decimal capacity. The balance preserves acquired capacity and recorded vacancies, linking refinement and the tritic regime. This capacity reading does not replace the full dynamics of TPK.

rows.name: π, φ, and e · Three Readings of the Same Process
rows.explanation: Coinductive generation determines π, φ, and e by prolonging the same process to arbitrary depth: every refinement preserves what has been constructed and adds resolution. For π, one transverse, three positive, and one negative region converge to the ternary sequence 010211, with multiplicities 432 + 4 × 144 = 1,008. The marked flag links these regions to four residual octads and one transverse octad of the Witt star. Modal incidence determines φ and compatible propagation determines e. The finite verification covers 396 levels, 2,376 trits, 43 turns, and 387 equal-phase pairs per channel, retaining orientation, carry, and memory together. Analytic characterizations subsequently recognize the generated constants.

rows.name: Imaginary Unit and Refinement
rows.explanation: The negative-square operator realizes complex orientation. The ternary update increases resolution without erasing the preceding levels.

rows.name: α · Closure with Carry and Analytic Reading
rows.explanation: Exceptional–temporal selection fixes the coupling record. The first route normalizes remainders and carries; the second completes the vacancy reader with the same pre-coordinate. Compatibility establishes αA = αB. The coefficient λ is constructed from that pre-coordinate: these are not two independent fits.

tables.title: Action and the Algebraic Structure of the Electron
tables.intro: Action and the electron evaluation are presented with their complete factors, following the dependency order of the corpus. Sources: articles I, II, and VI.

rows.name: Reduced Planck Constant · Action before Return
rows.explanation: H₅ combines the contributions of α and φ in the action reading before return. Its dimensional realization first gives reduced action ℏpre; a complete turn supplies the factor 2π and produces hpre. The subscript pre identifies this orientation of the trajectory.

rows.name: Regional Return and Action Ratio
rows.explanation: Five emissions retain the terminal block (169, 272, 272) four times and its alternative once. Within the persistent block, the coordinate distinguished under its preserving permutations selects 169. Word length supplies degree six, and the transport determinant generates the regional continuation. This determines Cπ and hence the returned action ηret. Ract compares outward and return readings: its excess over one, approximately 6.93 × 10⁻¹⁰, measures an internal asymmetry that enters the mass law through state-specific exponents.

rows.name: Reduced Planck Constant · Returned Action
rows.explanation: The subscript ret denotes the returning trajectory. This section transports the regional contribution that distinguishes the two orientations and is used in the gravitational evaluation shown here.

rows.name: Planck · Common Scale of Outward and Return Action
equations: $\hbar_{\rm geom}=\sqrt{\hbar_{\rm pre}\hbar_{\rm ret}},\qquad h_{\rm geom}=2\pi\hbar_{\rm geom}$
$\hbar_{\rm pre}=\hbar_{\rm geom}e^\xi,\quad\hbar_{\rm ret}=\hbar_{\rm geom}e^{-\xi},\quad\xi=\frac{1}{2}\log R_{\rm act}$
rows.explanation: The geometric mean separates the common action scale from the orientation of return. It is the parametrization developed in the integral corpus, equation (36.14); the two orientations remain explicit. Reduced action is given first, and multiplication by 2π then gives the action of a complete turn.

rows.name: Electron · Complete Evaluation Expression
rows.explanation: Projector incompatibility contributes √3/4; torsional normalization and the return incorporate the profile (80, 54, 6). With uE = 1 MeV, the coordinate is realized as energy and mass. The complete numerical comparison appears in the metrological table.

rows.name: Mass Operator and Organization of States
rows.explanation: Mass is obtained from the persistent organization of the state: route, orientation, occupation and memory determine its signature. M⁽⁰⁾ is the initial mass form; B records the response to return and Ract transmits the action ratio already constructed. Applying the same factor on both sides preserves a positive mass operator. Its evaluation on each state produces the corresponding scalar reading. The 81 cells, 56 route sets, 13 multisections and 324 oriented conditions organize this domain; links and boundaries are preserved before the signature is extracted.

tables.title: Length, Planck Scales, and Gravitational Coupling
tables.intro: The marked length is constructed before G. Action and the conjugate readings of the same positive character determine its coupling. Speed retains its constitutive provenance c = ĉ uC; dimensional bases are restored only once.

rows.name: Planck Length and Gravitational Coupling
equations: $H\Lambda=\hbar_a c I,\quad R\Lambda=L_\alpha^2 I,\quad M=H/c^2,\quad R=GM/c^2$
rows.explanation: The observed return contributes (N−1)/(4N); the complement 1/(4N) remains in memory. Longitudinal composition with α¹⁶ fixes Lα before G is evaluated. Energy and radial response preserve the same character: the two product identities fix their proportionality. The reduced gravitational-radius reading R = GM/c² then determines a unique G in this realization. With L* = 1 m, ℏret = ηret × 10⁻³⁴ J s, and c = 299,792,458 m/s, one obtains the displayed values. The circular expression is recovered with t₀ = πLα/(54c); the factor 54/π is not applied to Lα a second time.

rows.name: Radial Readings and Scales of the Same Character
rows.explanation: On a positive, invertible finite-dimensional fibre, the readings preserve HΛ = ℏacI and RΛ = Lα²I. For y > 0, they give m = mP,a y, rg = Lαy, and λ̄ = Lα/y. Equality of the two lengths characterizes y = 1, the circular specialization of the construction. The Schwarzschild radius is 2rg. Changing the action section by a factor ρ multiplies mP and EP by ρ, divides G by ρ, and preserves Lα and tP. The null sector retains its separate treatment.

rows.name: Boltzmann Constant · From Tritic Decision to Energy
rows.explanation: The uniform ternary decision has three equiprobable alternatives, whose information is log 3. The 108-step cycle supplies duration; the constructed action converts its frequency into energy. Thus εa/log 3 is energy per unit of information. The index a preserves outward or return orientation. Information, action, length, and propagation are connected before temperature is expressed in kelvin.

rows.name: Boltzmann · Spectral Reference and Thermometric Selection
rows.explanation: Comparing 729 tritic words with 1000 decimal positions fixes a capacity: after the first vacancy, the marked return has C₂₄ = 23. Twenty labels produce 20 × 19 = 380 off-diagonal relations; twenty-five positions and twenty-four adjacencies produce 25² + 24 = 649 records. The realization assigns these sectors, together with the rank-one vacuum, to degrees 23, 26, and 29 of a reference with ratio 1/10. Their relative weight gives b*. The instrument retains the complement and permits recovery of the state. Information per reference and energy conditioned on the sector form the thermal pair: additivity fixes the former, and for a finite nonscalar Hamiltonian their differential ratio determines temperature and transducer. Cut, grading, and the pair of readings specify the realization. The cycle supplies log 3 while preserving action, area, and gravitation.
rows.value: Coefficient of the marked realization: b* = 1.380649 × 10⁻²³.

tables.title: Area, Information, and Quantum Mixing
tables.intro: The transition from hexad to octad preserves incidence relations and distinguishes sectorial composition and entropy. Sources: monographs II and X. The experimental CKM comparisons appear in the final metrological tables.

rows.name: Barbero–Immirzi and the 90/120 Incidences
rows.explanation: A and C* are angular coordinates expressed in degrees; ΔSₙ = Sₙ(q−) − Sₙ(q+). The sectors of 90 and 120 configurations arise from the hexad and octad incidences.

rows.name: CKM Angles and the CP Phase
rows.explanation: A, C*, and Δ are expressed in degrees, with Δ = (180/π)Δ₄. The rational matrix relating the coordinates has determinant −3857/6: it allows the initial coordinates to be reconstructed from the mixing angles within the stated representation.

rows.name: Meaning of Mixing and Angular Agreement
rows.explanation: The three angles determine mixing between generations; the CP phase and Jarlskog invariant express its complex asymmetry. All five evaluations lie within the PDG 2025 reference intervals used here. In particular, the calculated phase 65.676173° is compared with 65.718259° ± 1.489690°. The final tables give both the sines and angles in degrees. Electroweak W/Z mixing is a distinct reading, displayed separately.

rows.name: Area and Entanglement Entropy
rows.explanation: The construction retains area, sectorial distribution, and boundary information together. These data distinguish equal-area configurations and articulate the readings of Barbero–Immirzi, entanglement, and mixing. Area measures geometrical extent; entropy records the distribution of the reduced state. Ghosh–Mitra supplies a second theoretical state-counting construction with which to compare γ.

tables.title: Transport, Electromagnetic Constitution, and Statistics
tables.intro: The constitutive quantities arise from oriented transport; the occupation distributions arise from state completions. Sources: articles II, III, and V.

rows.name: Catalan and the Reciprocal Pell Section
rows.explanation: The double moment of the resolvent generates Catalan’s constant; the Pell section preserves two reciprocal factors of the same transport. Its full function enters the electromagnetic constitution: with D = s d/ds, D²C₂(s) = s/(1+s²) and f(s) = (1−s³)/(1−s⁴) = (1+s+s²)D²C₂(s)/[s(1+s)]. The two channels are r± = f(q±³⁰). The inverse equation and the limit C₂(0) = 0 recover the oriented function, not only its extremal value.

rows.name: Permittivity, Permeability, Impedance, and Speed
rows.explanation: The 90/120 incidences fix the eigenvalues of the two channels. All four internal coefficients are calculated. To express them in farads per metre, newtons per ampere squared, ohms, and metres per second, the formulas use the units of action uS, charge uQ, and speed uC. The integral corpus also evaluates μ₀, ε₀, and Z₀ in SI units from α_HMT and the defining coordinates of action, charge, and speed; their values and the CODATA references are presented together in the numerical tables. The relations με = c⁻² and μ/ε = Z² are preserved.

rows.name: Charge and Electrical Quanta
rows.explanation: The construction links charge, resistance, conductance, flux, and the Josephson constant, preserving RK G₀ = 2 and KJ Φ₀ = 1.

rows.name: Bose–Einstein, Fermi–Dirac, and Radiation
rows.explanation: The symmetric and exterior completions generate bosonic and fermionic occupations. Their electromagnetic realization leads to the Planck spectrum and the Stefan–Boltzmann and Wien relations.

tables.title: Relations between Constants and Restitution of Transformations
tables.intro: Monograph VII connects the readings of action, propagation, and mass through their common operations. The inverse relations recover outputs already constructed and preserve orientation, domain, and dimensional reference.

rows.name: Constitutive Compatibility and Reconstruction Sensitivity
rows.explanation: In the normalized constitutive domain, speed fixes the product of the responses, and the Barbero–Immirzi functional distinguishes their oriented partition. Together, these data determine the labelled eigenvalues of the two channels. The logarithms of speed and impedance are derivatives of the same spectral potential; its Hessian characterizes the sensitivity of the inversion. Catalan’s function and the constitutive function are recovered through a second-order differential equation with a condition at the origin. The spectral moment, arguments, and orientation are preserved jointly; the isolated decimal value of Catalan’s constant does not replace them.

rows.name: Relative Transport and Restitution of Action
rows.explanation: Quarter-turns of conjugate elliptic forms produce a unimodular loop with reciprocal dilations. The stated branch and orientation allow the dimensionless action coefficient to be recovered. Closing the phase balance does not erase the imprint of the order of operations. Restoring a dimensional action additionally requires its scale to be preserved; conservation of symplectic area is not equivalent to an energy gain.

rows.name: Mass, Frequency, Geometric Reciprocity, and Thermal Reading
rows.explanation: Under the specified circular and thermal conditions, a positive mass coordinate determines four readings. The two lengths dilate reciprocally and preserve the product R108²; the thermal cycle contributes the weighting 3^(−ΞΓ). The identity retains the mass constructor, its normalizations, and the convergence conditions: it does not identify different physical realizations without them.

tables.title: Gravitation, Memory, and Cosmological Dynamics
tables.intro: The coupling constructed from the marked length enters the gravitational response. Action reciprocity preserves the area, and material memory contributes the explicit torsional amplitude. Sources: monographs II and VIII and the joint development of length, memory, and gravitation.

rows.name: Memory and Torsional Amplitude
rows.explanation: Eliminating contorsion produces the matter amplitude. In the occupation-three sector, Qsp = 4I preserves positivity. Memory determines dilution with the sixth power of the spatial scale.

rows.name: Regular Transition from Contraction to Expansion
rows.explanation: For spatially flat dust, a vanishing effective cosmological constant, and c = 1, the scale reaches a positive minimum and the solution is regular at all times. The document proves causal completeness in this domain and separately studies local persistence under perturbations.

tables.title: Coupling, Symmetries, and Closure of the Continuum
tables.intro: Numerical determination and exceptional incidence are readings of the same construction. Sources: monographs IV, XI, and XII.

rows.name: Exceptional–Temporal Determination
rows.explanation: The selector traverses 19,446 candidates in the terminal domain; 79 satisfy exceptional compatibility, and one also satisfies the temporal condition. Hadamard inversion recovers the selected record in another representation: recovery and selection perform distinct functions within the same construction.

rows.name: Conservation and Reversibility of Information
rows.explanation: The bilateral law and the infinite archive preserve the norm and allow the state to be reconstructed. Phase return does not erase memory: restitution depends on preserving the relations of the complete sequence.

rows.name: Marked Incidence, Leech, Moonshine, and M-Theory
rows.explanation: The Witt flag organizes the gluing, and the marked vector of squared norm 54 determines the rootless Leech neighbour. The vertex operator construction leads to the Moonshine module, with the Monster as its automorphism group. The constant’s record also determines a nonzero direction: its complement fixes the reduction 11 → 10 after the uniform mode is removed in 12 → 11. This polarization is coordinated with the 26 → 24 screen and T-duality. The prolongation towards M-theory transports the action and the identity Q² = H through the stated isometries and domains; the physical identification preserves the specific conditions of that realization.

rows.name: Real Line and Internal Cardinal Classification
rows.explanation: Compatible cylinders construct the line without introducing it as an initial datum. Genealogical closure prolongs the record through subsets definable with parameters already produced. Condensation assigns ordinal codes to the internal reals; the coding of countable well-orders and their ternary lifting construct the inverse injection. Cantor–Bernstein establishes cardinal equality. The classification covers the internal subsets of this line: infinite subsets are countable or equinumerous with the constructed continuum. The domain preserves the memory of its construction and the two projections from which it arises.

tables.intro: The kernel extends through distinct readers of the same structure. Residues and torsion determine characters; their moments produce spectral constants. Regularization preserves the finite parts of those moments. Compatible cylinders then allow resolutions and information rates to be compared. The recognized formulas come at the end of these constructions. Sources: the integral corpus, chapters 41–45, and the systematic treatise.

tables.intro: Each row compares the same quantity in the same units. Δ is evaluation minus reference; Δ/u expresses the difference in units of the stated uncertainty. Exact SI references have zero uncertainty, so that quotient is not defined.
tables.note: The reciprocal 1/α is compared directly with the same CODATA quantity. Against 2018, the relative difference is 7.78924 × 10⁻³⁵; the experimental uncertainty of 1/α is 2.1 × 10⁻⁸. The tabulated decimal α = 0.0072973525693(11) is rounded: its absolute difference is 1.61990 × 10⁻¹⁴ and is not a separate measurement. The electron uses uE = 1 MeV. Sources: I, VI, and NIST/CODATA 2018 and 2022.

tables.title: Boltzmann · Spectral Construction and Thermal Reading
tables.intro: The coefficient is obtained as a relative intensity of the marked spectral reference. The thermal reading combines information per reference and conditioned energy; their derivative fixes temperature in the transported bases.
tables.note: The comparison uses uE = 1 J and uΘ = 1 K; both columns therefore express energy per unit temperature. The numerical coefficient b* comes from the spectral realization described above. Ranks 1, 380, and 649, degrees 23 + 3n, and the rank-one reference specify the realization. Within it, additivity and conditioning determine the transducer and the free-energy minimum. The number exactly matches the SI numeral of Boltzmann’s constant; the physical identification retains these operations and the energy and temperature bases. Source: II, marked thermal composition and reading instrument; the SI reference is used after evaluation.

tables.title: CKM Mixing and the Barbero–Immirzi Coefficient
tables.intro: The five calculated CKM coordinates lie within the PDG 2025 reference intervals. Sines, CP phase, and Jarlskog invariant are compared in the same parametrization. Barbero–Immirzi is shown with the theoretical Ghosh–Mitra reference. Δ denotes evaluation minus reference.
tables.note: Sources: article II and the PDG 2025 CKM review, equations (12.27)–(12.28). Δ/u uses the published uncertainty on the side selected by the sign of Δ. The sines are matrix parameters; matrix elements also contain cosine factors. For γ, the relative difference from Ghosh–Mitra is −2.15953 × 10⁻⁴; this reference follows from its state-counting equation.

tables.title: CKM Angles Expressed in Degrees
tables.intro: To make the angular comparison explicit, the same coordinates as in the preceding table are expressed in degrees. The θ references are obtained by applying arcsin to the PDG 2025 sines; the CP phase is converted from radians. These are not additional measurements.
tables.note: The figures are rounded only for presentation. Angular uncertainties are obtained by transforming the endpoints of the published intervals; degrees are not identified with sines. Source: PDG 2025, CKM review, equations (12.27)–(12.28).

tables.title: Electroweak Angular Reading and the On-Shell Reference
tables.intro: W and Z share the counter-angle and differ by one angle unit. Their angular ratio retains exp(−x), while the complete signatures also contain Δ₄, s₁₂₀, and ζ₂₇₀. Subtracting (94, −1, 0, −2, 4) and (95, −1, −11, 0, −4) preserves these terms and changes the ratio. Electroweak mixing is distinct from CKM mixing.
tables.note: The second row uses the complete-signature masses in the final table: mW = 80378.964909704547… and mZ = 91187.533444313408… MeV/c². On-shell defines sW² = 1 − MW²/MZ² for physical masses in that convention; the PDG fit includes radiative effects. The differences are 16.1209 and −4.52478 reference uncertainties. They are numerical distances; the physical comparison retains the signature realization and pole or resonance convention. The angular determinant does not replace the complete mass ratio. Sources: VI, the narrative W/Z section, and PDG 2025 §§10.2 and 10.4.5.

tables.title: Electromagnetic Constants in SI Units
tables.intro: The HMT evaluation and the references are expressed in the same units. Both CODATA editions are retained to show the agreement with 2018 and the change in the 2022 adjustment. Δ means evaluation minus reference.
tables.note: The documented realization uses α_HMT and the exact defining values of the SI: h_SI = 6.62607015 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, e_SI = 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and c_SI = 299792458 m/s. Here e_SI is the elementary charge. CODATA enters subsequently, as a reference; the three electromagnetic comparisons depend on the same evaluation of α. Equality of c expresses the adopted SI convention, not an independent prediction. The normalized coefficients of the constitutive derivation are not compared directly with dimensional quantities. Sources: integral corpus, p. 119, and NIST/CODATA 2018–2022. Parentheses indicate standard uncertainty.

The first equation corresponds to F/Fc; the second to A, with a basal normalization distinct from the electron beta normalization.
